svg.title: One Deployment, four states — what each toleration actually bought

g.text: One Deployment, four states — what each toleration actually bought
STATE 1 · nodeSelector alone is not enough
STATE 2 · add a NoSchedule toleration
STATE 3 · a second taint, this time NoExecute
STATE 4 · add the second toleration
THE FILTER, AS THE DOCUMENTATION STATES IT
NODE worker-2 taints: custom-taint1=lenient:NoSchedule
POD tolerations: none
POD nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/hostname: worker-2
STATUS: Pending NODE: none
nodeSelector narrowed the candidates to exactly one node. The taint then removed
that one node. Two INDEPENDENT filters, and the Pod has to pass both.
kubectl describe pod → FailedScheduling: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint
POD tolerations:
- key: custom-taint1 · operator: Exists · effect: NoSchedule
STATUS: Running NODE: worker-2
Nothing attracted the Pod to worker-2 — nodeSelector had already done that and was
being blocked. The toleration only REMOVED THE OBJECTION. operator: Exists means
'any value for this key', so the taint's value never had to be written down.
kubectl taint node worker-2 custom-taint2=strict:NoExecute
NODE worker-2 taints: custom-taint1=lenient:NoSchedule ← still tolerated
custom-taint2=strict:NoExecute ← NOT tolerated
The RUNNING Pod is EVICTED. Its replacement is Pending.
This is the NoSchedule / NoExecute difference, live: NoSchedule would have left the
running Pod alone and only blocked new ones. NoExecute does both — and the Deployment
dutifully creates a replacement that cannot be placed either.
POD tolerations:
- key: custom-taint1 · operator: Exists · effect: NoSchedule
- key: custom-taint2 · operator: Equal · value: strict · effect: NoExecute
STATUS: Running NODE: worker-2
operator: Equal needs the VALUE spelled out — 'strict' — where Exists did not.
One toleration per taint: the filter leaves nothing un-ignored, so nothing objects.
Start with ALL of a node's taints, then IGNORE the ones the Pod has a matching
toleration for. The remaining UN-IGNORED taints have the indicated effects:
at least one un-ignored NoSchedule → will NOT schedule onto that node
no NoSchedule but one PreferNoSchedule → will TRY not to schedule there
at least one un-ignored NoExecute → EVICTED if already running there,
and will not be scheduled there
A toleration does not cancel a taint for everyone — it excuses ONE Pod from ONE taint.
add toleration 1
admin taints the node again
add toleration 2

State 1 is the one worth predicting before running it: nodeSelector points the Pod at the node, and the taint still refuses it. The result is Pending, not Failed — the scheduler keeps retrying forever.
Every state above is one line of YAML or one kubectl command apart from the next.
